findings.message: The code treats a set slot with no Time source as two different things. For a pinned line, `!sources.length` throws `unavailable` because Time isn't running. For the page history, `slotsSet()` is true, so the same empty source list returns `note: null` and the history reads as complete. When Time is switched off, any time lines already logged against the proposal drop out of the history with no note. Fix: return a note (for example "unread" or a new "off") whenever `sources.length === 0`, not only when the slots were never set. Use one rule for both paths, and test the page with `setProvided([])`.
findings.scenario: AMAX_MODULES_DISABLED=time, and CON-014 has logged time in core.audit_event. The proposal page shows no time lines and no note, which reads as 'none logged'. get_proposal_event for one of those time lines returns 503 unavailable.

findings.message: The owner-name rule (`ownerShownIn`) was applied to the list, the board, the proposal page and the update card. The Overview's 'Approve proposal' row still reads the raw `p.owner_name`. A proposal whose owner is set only as `owner_user_id` falls back to "Delivery" there. Fix: select `${ownerShownIn("p")}` in proposalsToApprove.
findings.scenario: A proposed proposal has owner_user_id = Maya and owner_name null. The Overview shows raisedBy "Delivery" while the list and board show "Maya Fernando".

findings.message: The stale message uses the raw `row.owner_name`. When the owner is a user with no stored name, accepting the suggestion fails with 'has an owner now (null)'. Use the owner-name rule or the user's name instead.
findings.scenario: owner_user_id is set and owner_name is null. Accepting the suggested owner fails with 'CON-1 has an owner now (null)'.

findings.message: The AC6 test's `finally` resets the module list to `["delivery","time"]` instead of the state it found. If no list was set before (`ids === null`, so the table check decides), later tests in the same worker run with an explicit list. Save the previous state and restore it, or reset to the unset state.
findings.scenario: A later test in this file depends on `hasModule` falling back to the table check. After AC6 it gets the forced list instead.

findings.message: The AC8 test only works because it runs first in the file, while `slotsSet()` is still false. `afterEach(setProvided([]))` sets the slots for good, and no API returns them to the unset state. Reordering the tests or running the file with `.only` breaks it. Add a test-only reset in installed.ts, or assert the unread state through an explicit reset.
findings.scenario: Move the AC8 test below AC6. `slotsSet()` is now true and the 'unread' expectation fails.
